clue.text: Deserted hollow

definitions.meaning: a deserted place has nobody in it
a hollow thing has nothing inside it

explanation.definitionFit: Both a vacant, abandoned place and a void-centred object contain nothing.

clue.text: Wild card?

definitions.meaning: wild here means odd or unconventional
a card is an amusingly odd person

explanation.definitionFit: Both an unconventional quality and an oddball person can be described with this word.

clue.text: Might one be served a share of his lunch?

definitions.text: Might one be served a share of his lunch?

parts.words: Might one be served a share of his lunch?
parts.note: a pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle is named after a farm worker; a share of his would be his lunch, and a share is also a plough blade

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a farmhand would hand out part of his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A share (ploughshare) is the blade of a plough, so the person working it might be 'served a share'. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman works the fields with a plough and gives his name to a classic British pub lunch.

clue.text: Lots of policemen always over the road

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old word meaning always

explanation.surface: Police are constantly patrolling across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AY into YA. The Yard is Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, used for the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yard is short for Scotland Yard, home of London's Metropolitan Police, so it stands for a body of officers.

clue.text: Notebook ideal for autumn?

definitions.meaning: a ring binder whose pages can be taken out and added is a ... notebook
in autumn the trees shed foliage, so a season of detached foliage would suit the description

explanation.surface: A stationery shop recommends a particular notebook for the autumn term.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder with removable pages is called looseleaf; read whimsically, autumn is the season when foliage comes free of trees.

clue.text: Florence help fat old Amy out?

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for Florence to help a portly elderly woman called Amy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HELPFATOLDAMY. Florence Nightingale was nicknamed the Lady of the Lamp for her night rounds in the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale, the nursing pioneer, earned this nickname walking the wards at night carrying a light.

clue.text: This quarter is Latin, admitting any leader

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Latin for is, as in id est, is est

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone declares that this district is Latin and open to any leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts A, the first letter of 'any' picked out by 'leader', inside EST.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass quarters.

clue.text: Crack tile perhaps on end of gable

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed below, so this piece follows the other
the end of a word is its last letter
perhaps hints at a possible variant, so the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder considers putting a cracked tile on the edge of a gable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a break in the tile, but it is the definition: crack troops are first-rate. In a down clue 'on' puts the rearranged tile below the gable's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack troops are top-quality, the best of the best.

clue.text: Dickensian scoundrel with cigarette burning

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
a fire that is still burning is said to be in

explanation.surface: A villain from Dickens smoking a lit cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the villainous leader of child pickpockets in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Singers in church knocking back port

indicators.note: knocking back, like downing a drink, signals that the port's name is read backwards

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: Church singers are drinking port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' suggests drinking the port, but it reverses the Brazilian city's name; 'in' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of vocal performers, often in church.

clue.text: Garbo, the clue to this piece of jewellery

parts.note: the name splits as GARB, clothing or dress, plus O, a ring shape; so the answer read as an instruction, dress then ring, builds this name

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter teases that the film star Greta Garbo hints at a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is read as wordplay producing the clue word. DRESS gives GARB, RING gives O (the letter is round), together GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress ring is a showy ring worn for decoration rather than as an engagement band.

clue.text: Changing tenner meant it was fun

indicators.note: changing tells us these letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Breaking a ten-pound note into change was enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges TENNERMEANTIT; a tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment is amusement or enjoyment, which is what fun means.

clue.text: Near dark, but not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: dark is another word for night-time

explanation.surface: It is almost dark, but not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not quite' cuts the final T from NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word meaning close by.

clue.text: Fabulous number of peculators?

parts.note: peculators are embezzlers or thieves; the fable of Ali Baba gives a fixed count of thieves in the cave

explanation.surface: How many embezzlers there are is said to be legendary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means 'from a fable', not 'wonderful': Ali Baba faced forty thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: In the tale of Ali Baba the band of thieves numbers forty, a count found in a fable.

clue.text: None put out the light

indicators.note: put out suggests letters disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody switched off the lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like extinguishing the light but rearranges NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon gas glows in signs and tubes, so it serves as a kind of lighting.

clue.text: Note car carrying maiden over

indicators.note: carrying here means the car takes the other piece with it, attached alongside

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
M is the scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over in cricket, one with no runs

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a car is taking a young woman across.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden over is one in which no runs are scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets, a half note.

clue.text: Boundary of motorway, illuminated all round

indicators.note: all round means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: illuminated means lit up
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: The edge of the motorway is lit up all the way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a major British motorway, read in crosswords as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the edge beyond which something may not go.

clue.text: 8 as backing group for European song contest

definitions.text: 8 as backing group for European song contest

parts.words: 8 as backing group for European song contest
parts.note: 8 refers to the answer at 8 across, singers; the German guild of master singers held song contests, as in Wagner's opera set in Nuremberg

explanation.surface: A choir is booked to provide backing vocals at the Eurovision Song Contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Eurovision; the real contest is the singing competition of Wagner's Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg.
explanation.definitionFit: A Meistersinger was a member of a German guild of poet-musicians who competed in song.

clue.text: Pop and egg in real spread

indicators.note: spread suggests letters scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A recipe involves spreading egg on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges EGGINREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink, which is what pop means.

clue.text: Broadcast event in which baton is handed over

definitions.text: Broadcast event in which baton is handed over

parts.note: to relay is to transmit or broadcast
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A televised athletics event where runners pass a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while two of its words build it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay race team members each run a leg, passing a baton on.

clue.text: Fee for analysis?

definitions.meaning: in law a payment given in return for a promise
careful thought given to a question

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a payment made in a contract and the careful thought given to a matter.

clue.text: Bond's swearword

explanation.surface: James Bond has a favourite curse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a sworn pledge and a curse uttered in anger.

clue.text: Scotch governor at the end of a bottle

definitions.text: Scotch governor at the end of a bottle

parts.words: Scotch governor at the end of a bottle
parts.note: a device fixed to the neck of an upturned spirits bottle in a bar regulates how much whisky is poured

explanation.surface: A Scottish ruler reaches the bottom of a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like a nationality but is whisky; 'governor' is a regulating device. An optic is the measuring nozzle on bar spirits bottles in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is a bar device attached to an inverted bottle to dispense a fixed measure of spirits.

clue.text: Time called in bars

parts.note: suggests last orders at a pub, but bars are units of music, and the pace of music is set by a marking

explanation.surface: The barman calls time in the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs and 'Time called' like closing time, but bars are musical measures and the speed is marked on the score.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed at which music is played, its time.

clue.text: State principal point

parts.note: principal means main or chief
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone states their chief argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Extremely light flare

definitions.meaning: a ... light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: A flare burns extremely brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means highly, and also names the Very light, a signal flare named after its inventor.

clue.text: Regretfully, a girl lost a shilling

indicators.note: lost means a piece has gone missing from the rest

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
S was the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money

explanation.surface: Sadly, a girl mislaid a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes one S from A LASS. A shilling was an old British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of sorrow or regret.

clue.text: Date when Caesar collected his rents?

definitions.text: Date when Caesar collected his rents?

parts.words: Date when Caesar collected his rents?
parts.note: rents looks like money owed by tenants, but means tears or stab wounds; Julius Caesar was stabbed to death on a famous date in March

explanation.surface: Asking on which day the Roman landlord gathered tenants' payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rents' means tears, the stab wounds Caesar received when assassinated on 15 March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was the mid-month day of the Roman calendar; Caesar was murdered on the Ides of March.

clue.text: Such long-range photography shows petal semi-opening

indicators.note: opening, as a bud does, signals that the letters unfold into a new order

explanation.surface: Slow-motion footage shows a flower's petals half opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' rearranges PETALSEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-lapse photography compresses a long span of time, such as a flower opening, into seconds.

clue.text: Doctor takes a morning back in theatre

indicators.note: back tells us the morning abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: AM stands for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A doctor goes back into the operating theatre one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AM into MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is the art of the stage, so it stands for theatre as a field.

clue.text: Lookout! It may contain high tars

definitions.meaning: a lookout post at the top of a ship's mast
tars are sailors, and up the mast the lookout platform holds them

explanation.surface: A warning shout about something holding lofty sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow's nest is the lookout platform high on a ship's mast where sailors keep watch.

clue.text: "Carry-on" location

definitions.meaning: a fuss or display of temper

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a public fuss and the place where an event happens.
